RE-STAMPED AFTER THE enterprise REBASE, NUMBER UNCHANGED. enterprise replayed onto origin on 2026-09-04, so every SHA in it changed and the stamps written earlier the same day were orphaned within the hour. Re-measured at 401369e7fe3 in a clean detached worktree laid out beside a clean odoo worktree, as that lane lays it out, and it reads what the floor already said. This stamp names a enterprise commit, so an odoo rebase does not orphan it again.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

STAMP REFRESHED, NUMBER UNCHANGED. The old stamp named a commit the 2026-09-02 sync replayed away, so --list flagged it ORPHANED-BASE and the sibling architecture.yml exited 2 asking to be re-measured rather than comparing -- neither green nor red. Re-measured in a clean detached worktree of enterprise at f6fa11352db, laid out beside a clean odoo worktree exactly as the lane does, because these gates resolve the community fork as a sibling and reading one alone inflates the count: unresolved_calls_enterprise measured 11 pointed at the sibling on its own and 3 in the pair.

28 -> 26. THE FLOOR WAS RED IN THE FALLING DIRECTION and carried no `measured_at`, so nothing could say when it stopped being true. Re-measured on a clean detached worktree at the stamped commit -- python odoo/tooling/architecture/py_x2many_count.py --addon enterprise --count -- and it reads 26.

WHAT FELL CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED, and that is the cost of the missing stamp rather than an omission here: with no commit recorded there is no tree to diff the finding set against. The baseline file was last written by 876ba89f63b (2026-08-22); enterprise has moved since and nothing recorded where. A sibling floor's stamp is the SIBLING's commit, recorded through `--update --root enterprise` from a clean detached worktree of that checkout, so it resolves in the repository that was actually measured.
